territorial_scope.description: Applies within Utah to political subdivisions of the state and entities within them.

evidence.quote: A political subdivision of the state, or an entity within a political subdivision of the state, may not enact a law, ordinance, or rule governing the private use of an unmanned aircraft

summary.short: Amends Utah Code 72-14 on unmanned aircraft and advanced air mobility. Section 5 revises definitions, including advanced air mobility system and unmanned aircraft. Section 6 bars political subdivisions from regulating private use of such aircraft, except as authorized or by airport operators, and supersedes earlier local laws.
summary.long: This excerpt contains two sections of Utah's aviation amendments to Title 72, Chapter 14, which governs unmanned aircraft and advanced air mobility systems. Section 5 amends the chapter's definitions. It defines advanced air mobility system as a system that transports individuals and property using piloted and unpiloted aircraft, including electric and vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, and includes components such as remote and autonomous functions. It defines unmanned aircraft as an aircraft capable of sustaining flight with no possible direct human intervention, and unmanned aircraft system as the entire system used to operate one. Section 6 amends 72-14-103. A political subdivision or an entity within one may not enact a law, ordinance or rule governing private use of unmanned aircraft or advanced air mobility systems, unless the chapter authorizes it or an airport operator enacts it to govern operations within the airport or takeoff and landing there. Subsection (2) states that the chapter supersedes local laws or rules enacted before July 1, 2017. The excerpt sets out no penalties and gives no effective date.
